widgets_values:
A - CHUNKED PROCESSING

Long sequences are processed in fixed-size chunks so VRAM stays flat.

  Chunk index  (PrimitiveInt)   0, 1, 2, ...   mode: increment
  Chunk offset (MathExpression) index * CHUNK -> skip_first_frames
  Load Video   frame_load_cap = CHUNK

The number in the expression (a * 48) MUST match frame_load_cap.

Usage:
  1. set the chunk index back to 0
  2. enable Auto Queue and let it run through the sequence
  3. when done: reset the chunk index to 0 and turn Auto Queue off

Each run writes its own numbered batch of PNGs, so the chunks stay
in order on disk.

nodes.title: 8b. Color Curves - shape subject matte falloff

widgets_values:
SAM3 SOFT MATTE MASK - OVERVIEW

Text-prompted segmentation (SAM3) blended with a luma-derived soft
matte, written out as a PNG mask sequence. Built for pulling a small
detail (an eye, a highlight, a logo) out of longer footage.

  A  chunked frame loading - long footage in fixed-size chunks
  B  SAM3 checkpoint + two text prompts
  C  SAM3 detection -> grow / blur per branch
  D  optional luma soft matte from the source frames
  E  masks combined -> saved as a PNG sequence
  G  same mask as alpha on the source -> RGBA cut-out

Required custom nodes:
  ComfyUI-VideoHelperSuite  (VHS_LoadVideo, VHS_VideoCombine)
  ComfyUI-KJNodes           (GrowMaskWithBlur)
  WAS Node Suite            (Image Levels Adjustment)
  pythongosssss custom-scripts (MathExpression)
  ComfyUI_LayerStyle           (only for switch 5c)

Read the note inside each group before changing values.

B - MODEL + PROMPTS

Checkpoint: a SAM3 model placed in ComfyUI/models/checkpoints.

  Prompt A = the small detail to isolate   (e.g. "fish eye")
  Prompt B = the larger subject it sits on (e.g. "fish")

Short, concrete noun phrases work best. Lower the SAM3 threshold if
the detection drops out on some frames, raise it if it starts
grabbing the background.

C - DETECTION + EDGE SOFTENING

SAM3 Detect returns a hard mask per frame; GrowMaskWithBlur turns it
into something compositable.

  expand      dilate in pixels
  blur_radius feather in pixels

  detail branch  generous expand + blur - hides detection jitter
  subject branch almost no expand, 1 px blur - keeps the silhouette

individual_masks = false -> one merged mask per frame.
refine_iterations trades speed for edge accuracy.

D - LUMA SOFT MATTE (optional)

Builds a soft matte straight from the source frames:

  source -> R channel as mask -> back to image -> Levels -> mask

The Levels black / mid / white values decide how much of the bright
interior survives; this is what gives the final mask a gradient
instead of a hard cutout.

"Grow 1px" is bypassed (mode 4) by default - enable it if the edge
comes out too thin. Bypass this whole group if you only want the
plain SAM3 mask.

E - COMBINE + OUTPUT

Color Curves (subgraph) reshapes the subject matte falloff before it
is added in - flatten the RGB master curve to reduce its influence.

Both MaskComposite nodes use "add"; switch to "multiply" if you want
the intersection of the two masks instead of the union.

Save: 8-bit PNG sequence, filename_prefix = <subfolder>/<name>_
Files land in ComfyUI/output/<subfolder>/ ready to be imported as an
image sequence in a compositor.

MODE SWITCHES (LazySwitchKJ, KJNodes)

  4c  TARGET          off = detail prompt 2a
                      on  = whole subject prompt 2b
  5c  VITMATTE REFINE off = grow + blur (feathered hard edge)
                      on  = real alpha matting (group F)
  7b  LUMA SOFT MATTE adds the group D matte on top
  9b  SUBJECT SHAPE   adds the subject mask as a second operand
                      (pointless when 4c is on)

All default OFF -> detail prompt, grow + blur. Every input is lazy,
so an off branch is never executed.

Two useful presets:
  a small hard detail   4c off, 5c off
  a translucent subject 4c on,  5c on, 9b off

F - VITMATTE EDGE REFINE (switch 5c, off by default)

SAM3 gives a BINARY mask - segmentation is a per-pixel classification,
so there is no real alpha in it. VITMatte is a matting model: it takes
the SAM3 mask, builds a trimap around its edge (edge_erode /
edte_dilate) and regresses a CONTINUOUS alpha inside that band. This
is what actually resolves hair, fur, glass and translucency, as
opposed to just feathering a hard edge.

  off -> 5a grow + blur   (feathered hard edge, fast)
  on  -> 5v VITMatte      (true alpha, slow)

With the switch on, the grow+blur node is skipped: VITMatte takes the
RAW SAM3 mask, because it needs the un-feathered edge to build its
trimap from.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
REQUIREMENTS - this branch needs an extra node pack AND a model

1) Node pack: ComfyUI_LayerStyle (chflame163)
   ComfyUI Manager -> Custom Nodes Manager -> "LayerStyle"
   or: git clone https://github.com/chflame163/ComfyUI_LayerStyle
       into ComfyUI/custom_nodes/

2) Model: vitmatte-small-composition-1k (~100 MB)
   https://huggingface.co/hustvl/vitmatte-small-composition-1k/tree/main
   Download: config.json, model.safetensors,
             preprocessor_config.json
   Copy to:  ComfyUI/models/vitmatte/

   method = "VITMatte"         downloads the model itself on first
                               run (needs internet)
   method = "VITMatte(local)"  loads it from ComfyUI/models/vitmatte
                               (use this once step 2 is done)

   PyMatting and GuidedFilter need no model at all - GuidedFilter is
   the fast, edge-aware version of what group D does by hand.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
TUNING

  edge_erode / edte_dilate  width of the trimap band in px. Wider =
                            more room to solve, slower, more risk of
                            bleeding. 6/6 is a good start.
  black_point / white_point alpha clipping. Keep 0.01 / 0.99 to stay
                            soft; pull them in to harden the matte.
  max_megapixels            VITMatte downscales above this. 2.0 is
                            below HD - set 4.0 for 1920x1080, more
                            for 4K, at the cost of VRAM.
  device                    cpu works, just slowly.

VITMatte runs per frame and is the slowest node in this graph. Test
on a short chunk before queueing a whole sequence.

G - RGBA CUT-OUT (prep for a compositing workflow)

The mask branch (group E) saves the matte on its own. This branch
saves the CUT-OUT: the source frames with the final mask as the alpha
channel, i.e. transparent PNGs you can drop straight into a
compositing graph - ComfyUI_LayerStyle's ImageBlendAdvance, an
inpaint crop/stitch relight pass, or After Effects / Nuke.

  12  InvertMask   REQUIRED. ComfyUI's JoinImageWithAlpha does
                   alpha = 1.0 - mask internally, so without this
                   node the object comes out transparent and the
                   background opaque. This is not a bug, it is the
                   MASK convention: a mask marks a region, it is not
                   an alpha channel.
  13  JoinImageWithAlpha  RGB + alpha -> 4-channel image
  14  VHS_VideoCombine    writes it out

ALPHA IS STRAIGHT, NOT PREMULTIPLIED. ComfyUI does not multiply the
RGB by the alpha, so set your compositor to "straight / unmatted"
when you import. Interpreting straight alpha as premultiplied is what
produces dark fringes on soft edges.

FORMAT - all three keep the alpha:
  video/8bit-png    default. 8 bit RGBA, one PNG per frame.
  video/16bit-png   rgba64. Use it if the matte will be graded hard
                    afterwards - 8 bit soft edges band quickly.
  ProRes + profile 4444  one .mov with alpha instead of a sequence,
                    handy for a round trip through AE.

Not needed? Ctrl+M mutes this node - or mute node 11 instead if you
only want the cut-out and not the matte.

nodes.title: 4c. SWITCH 0 - TARGET: off = detail (2a) / on = whole subject (2b)

widgets_values:
SWITCH 0 - WHAT ARE WE MASKING?

  off  prompt 2a, the DETAIL      (e.g. "fish eye")
  on   prompt 2b, the WHOLE SUBJECT (e.g. "translucent fish")

Everything downstream - grow+blur or VITMatte, the luma matte, the
cut-out - works on whichever of the two you pick here. Lazy, so the
other SAM3 pass does not run.

WHY YOU WANT THIS WITH 5c ON:
a subject that is translucent all over, or has thin fins / fur /
strands, is the case a binary mask cannot represent at all. No amount
of grow+blur helps: the fin edge is not a soft EDGE, it is a large
area of partial transparency. That is precisely what a matting model
solves. Target = subject + 5c on + the RGBA cut-out in group G is the
combination to test that with.

NOTE: with the target set to subject, switch 9b (add subject shape)
becomes pointless - it would add the subject to itself. Leave 9b off.

The luma matte (7b) is worth a try here too: for a translucent body
the luminance IS roughly the opacity, which is the one case where
that branch is not a hack.
